$comment: Site Planner speed budgets (the speed round, NEW-3, 2026-10-31). Read by ui-audit/verify-planner-perf.mjs.
Measured on the grading harness (the owner's Concept A on the real Chehaw ground, ?owner=2), grading ON with proposed contours +
cut/fill + paper, a PRODUCTION build, the CPU throttled 4x, at 1913x1000 / DSF 2.15 (the owner's screen). Views: the scale bar
reading 500 / 125 / 50 ft. A number here is the CEILING; a number in `knownOver` is a budget the planner does NOT meet today —
it carries the item that owns closing it and a `ratchet` (the worst value measured when it was filed, plus a little room): the
guard fails if it gets WORSE than the ratchet, and prints the gap to the budget on every run. Moving a number is a product
decision argued on the item, never a nudge to make a run pass (PERCEPTUAL-PARITY's rule, applied to time).
THE RULE BEHIND THE COUNTS: no feature may add per-pointer-move work to the planner. A pan or a drag move rebuilds nothing —
no surface, no worker job, no picture re-encode — and commits React at most once per move.
